_about: Factory lift operator huts (task 4.50 phase 3), to the maker's op houses (measured on the owner's 1:50 terminal drawings and on photos of the built stations, kept locally, never in the repo): a flat-roofed panel box on four pipe posts, its glazed front and a deep canopy facing the chairs at the load or unload point, a tall-lite door and a tall window on the wall round the corner, a window in the other end wall too (so the operator sees up and down the line), a steel landing and stair. Three bands: a fascia (the top `fascia` of the walls, and the canopy) and a wainscot (floor frame to the window sill) in the lift's livery, light ribbed panels between. Millimetres. Frame: origin at the hut's centre in plan, on the load or unload level; u along the front (`footprint.length`), v from back to front (`footprint.width`) with +v toward the chairs, w up. Heights are from the floor, which stands `floor` above the origin. The door is in an end wall (`doorSide`, -u unless given: the hut's hand), `fromFront` back from the front corner; seen from behind, a -u door is at the right end and a +u door at the left. The hut follows the drive, not top or bottom: `large` (wider than deep: the operator along the glazed front, the drive's cabinets along the back wall) at a detachable's or gondola's drive station; `small` (2,870 wide, as drawn) at a detachable's return station and a fixed grip's drive station; `mini` (no drawing: photos) at a fixed grip's return station. Posts, stair and landing legs run on below the origin (`below`), so the hut stands on ground that falls away, as at a top station; the stair keeps its pitch all the way down, so the ground clips it at the right step wherever it stands. Placement (phase 6): a hut stands on the side of the lift where the chairs go up, its front toward them, with its door, landing and stair at the end away from the line; seen from the chairs, a bottom station's door is on the right and a top station's on the left. As built, the large hut is a top-station hand and the small and mini bottom-station ones; the game mirrors a hut where a station needs the other hand. Surface lifts use the T-bar's own hut and carpets theirs (lift kit). `common` holds what every hut shares; each entry of `variants` overrides it.

large._about: As built at a drive station (photos, kept locally): wider than deep, its long glazed side to the chairs. The whole front is three big panes; each end wall has a tall window at its front corner, so the operator sees the chairs coming and going; the drive's cabinets stand along the blank back wall; the door is in the end that faces the load or unload area, under a small awning; a steel landing at the door and a stair down along that wall; the back wall blank, the cabinets' conduits dropping under it. The depth is measured from photos (about 13 ft).
